rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Pollution is waste added faster than the environment can assimilate it. Air pollution from vehicles, industry, brick kilns and indoor biomass burning drives respiratory disease, the greenhouse effect, acid rain and photochemical smog, controlled by catalytic converters, scrubbers, cleaner fuels and afforestation.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Eutrophication sequence: nutrients → algal bloom → death and decay → oxygen used up → fish death.
Biomagnification: concentration rises at each step of the food chain for persistent fat-soluble substances.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Primary vs secondary pollutants:** primary are emitted directly (CO, SO₂); secondary form in air by reactions (ozone, PAN).  ·  **BOD vs DO:** BOD is the oxygen demanded by decomposers; DO is the oxygen actually available — high BOD means low DO.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Name the gases. 'Smoke' alone is too vague for sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides.  ·  Mention plastics under soil pollution. They are now a standard example beside pesticides.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Phewa Lake*** — creeping eutrophication from nutrient runoff.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified 2024 PYQs: air pollution 3m, BOD 2m, soil erosion 3m — all in this topic.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Write the eutrophication chain in order.  ·  Make a three-row table: air, water, soil, with one source and one control each.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** Name two secondary pollutants and how they form. **Answer.** **Ozone (O₃)** and **PAN (peroxyacetyl nitrate)** — both form in **photochemical smog** when primary pollutants (NOₓ and unburnt hydrocarbons from vehicles) react under strong sunlight. Neither is emitted directly; sunlight manufactures them in the air.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most-tested: the three 2024 short answers — air pollution, BOD, soil erosion with Nepal measures.

Fundamental Concepts · Term | Definition · **Pollutant** | Any substance or agent added to the environment that causes harmful effects · **Primary pollutant** | Emitted directly (CO, SO₂, dust) · **Secondary pollutant** | Formed in air by reactions (ozone, PAN in smog) · **BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand)** | Oxygen (mg/L) needed by microbes to decompose organic matter in water over 5 days at 20°C — a measure of organic pollution · **Eutrophication** |…  ·  3.1 Sources · Source | Pollutants · Vehicle exhaust | CO, NOₓ, hydrocarbons, lead · Industry and power plants | SO₂, particulates, CO₂ · Brick kilns (major in Nepal) | CO, SO₂, particulates · Burning of solid waste and crop residue | CO₂, CO, dioxins, smoke · Indoor cooking (biomass, kerosene) | CO, particulates — a major household killer

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **BOD is the pollution meter:** the 2024 2m question — high BOD starves water of dissolved oxygen and aquatic life suffocates.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Air: vehicles/industry/kilns → CO, SO₂, NOₓ, particulates → respiratory disease, greenhouse effect, acid rain, smog; control by catalytic converters, scrubbers, cleaner fuels.  ·  Water: sewage, industry (heavy metals), fertiliser runoff → high BOD, eutrophication, biomagnification, pathogens; control by primary–secondary–tertiary sewage treatment.  ·  Soil: excess fertiliser/pesticide, erosion of topsoil by water/wind; Nepal measures — terracing, community forestry, cover crops, check dams, controlled grazing.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Lichens die where SO₂ is high — bioindicators of air quality.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Fish die in a eutrophic lake mainly because → B  ·  Biomagnification is best shown by → A
